name: Sela Dray
role: Iresh local guide and settlement liaison; early thirties. Survives Book 1. Knows weather, paths, chimes, taboo ground. Refuses Force theory; speaks in survival rules. Climax job: saves Tavi and locals through local knowledge Ben does NOT have. Calls Ben 'Skywalker' through Ch 28; shifts to 'Ben' from Ch 34 onward — conditional trust only.

three_dimensions.surface: Sela is a practical Iresh local guide/liaison who knows weather, paths, taboo ground, chimes, and what offworlders break when they arrive with causes. She does not explain the Force. She explains survival.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: That Tavi died because she could not stop him from needing money, opportunity, or approval. She dislikes Ben and Talon as offworlders but recognizes they may be the only tools available to stop worse offworlders.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Turns worry into irritation. Refuses mystical language. Gives rules instead of explanations. Treats Jedi questions as offworlder overcomplication. Weather, footing, chime lines, path markers, reed movement, who is ignoring warnings, who looks at landscape like property. Do not make her a mystical guide. Her authority comes from lived local knowledge.

voice_notes:
Practical, blunt, grounded. Never mystical unless quoting local phrasing, and even then she undercuts it.

Good Sela: “If the chimes stop, run. You can argue about what it means after you are not dead.” “That is the route offworlders built. It is not the same thing as the way out.” “You people always ask what it means. It means don’t go down there.” “You saved him. That does not make this place yours.” “Tavi knew better. That is what makes me angry.” Avoid Sela saying: “The Glasswell is a sacred place of memory.” Better: “Some places remember too loudly. Locals call that a warning. Offworlders call it research.”

Dry, local, unimpressed. She is funny because she refuses awe.

Blunt, wary, practical. Anger appears before fear.

Do not make her a mystical guide. Her authority comes from lived local knowledge.
thematic_role: Tests the theme as the local who refuses awe and refuses ownership. Thanks Ben for saving Tavi without granting Ben her home. Survival rules, not Force theory. The clearest argument in the book that the people Ben moves through are not props to his education.
avoid_list: Do not write theme as thesis.
Do not make dialogue interchangeable with other cast members.
